items.title: Air Canada halts Cuba flights as fuel crisis deepens

featured_image.name: Air Canada suspends flights to Cuba because of aviation fuel shortage

items.description:
Cuba enacted drastic emergency measures on Monday as the island nation grapples with a rapidly worsening energy crisis exacerbated by U.S. pressure to cut off its oil supply. The government has mandated a four-day workweek for state-owned companies, reduced school hours, suspended university classes, and slashed public transportation services while restricting fuel sales.[1][2][3][4]

The emergency protocols took effect as Havana's streets fell notably silent, with the communist government scrambling to preserve rapidly depleting fuel reserves. Air Canada announced Monday it is suspending all flights to Cuba after Cuban authorities warned that aviation fuel would no longer be available at the island's airports beginning Tuesday, February 10.[5][6][4]

items.title: Israel warns US it may strike Iran alone over missile threat

featured_image.name: Netanyahu to meet Trump in Washington Wednesday to discuss ...

items.description:
Israeli defense officials have told their American counterparts that Jerusalem is prepared to launch unilateral military strikes against Iran's ballistic missile infrastructure if Tehran crosses what Israel considers a critical security threshold, according to multiple reports citing security sources.

"We told the Americans we will strike alone if Iran crosses the red line we set on ballistic missiles," a senior Israeli source told The Jerusalem Post, adding that Israel has not yet reached that threshold but is continuously monitoring developments inside Iran. The officials described Iran's expanding missile capabilities as an existential threat and outlined operational plans to dismantle key manufacturing sites and production facilities.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Alphabet raises $20B in bond sale amid record AI-driven demand

featured_image.name: 2+ Hundred Alphabet Inc Headquarters Royalty-Free Images ...

items.description:
Alphabet, the parent company of Google, sold $20 billion in bonds on Monday in a deal that attracted more than $100 billion in investor orders, underscoring the enormous appetite for debt tied to the artificial intelligence boom.[1][2]

The seven-part offering of senior unsecured notes exceeded the company's initial expectations of $15 billion, with demand described by Bloomberg as among the strongest ever for a corporate bond offering. Alphabet is also planning an additional sterling bond sale that may include a rare 100-year "century bond," which would mark the first such long-dated debt issued by a technology company since the dot-com era.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: Cuba halts airline refueling for a month amid energy crisis

featured_image.name: Airlines will no longer be able to refuel on Cuba as U.S. blockade ...

items.description:
Cuba has notified international carriers that aviation fuel will be unavailable across the island's airports for an entire month, forcing major airlines to suspend or reroute flights as the nation's energy crisis reaches a critical stage.

The Cuban government issued an official Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) on Sunday evening warning that Jet A-1 fuel will not be available from February 10 through March 11 at all nine international airports, including Havana's José Martí International Airport, Varadero, Santa Clara, Holguín, Santiago de Cuba, and Cayo Coco. The measure is expected to disrupt more than 400 scheduled weekly flights.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Bennu asteroid samples challenge theory on how life's building blocks formed

featured_image.name: Life's ingredients have been found in samples from asteroid ...

items.description:
Amino acids, the molecular building blocks essential for life, may have formed in icy, radiation-rich conditions at the edge of the early solar system rather than in warm water, according to new research published today in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The findings, based on analysis of samples from asteroid Bennu returned to Earth by NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission in 2023, challenge decades of assumptions about how life's basic ingredients first arose.

"Our results flip the script on how we have typically thought amino acids formed in asteroids," said Allison Baczynski, assistant research professor of geosciences at Penn State and co-lead author of the study. "It now looks like there are many conditions where these building blocks of life can form, not just when there's warm liquid water."[1][2]

items.title: Mexico suspends oil shipments to Cuba to avoid US tariffs

featured_image.name: Mexico to send oil to Cuba despite Trump pressure - Bloomberg

items.description:
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum confirmed on Monday that Mexico has suspended oil shipments to Cuba to avoid tariffs threatened by the Trump administration, calling the US sanctions "very unfair" as she warned that the measures would "strangle" the crisis-stricken island nation.

"This sanction being imposed on countries that sell oil to Cuba is very unfair... sanctions that harm the people are not right," Sheinbaum told reporters at her daily press briefing. "You cannot strangle a people like this—it's very unfair, very unfair."[1]

items.title: Trump to visit China in April for Xi summit

featured_image.name: Trump, Xi discuss Taiwan and soybeans in call aimed at easing China, US relations

items.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump will travel to Beijing during the first week of April for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to a Politico report citing three people familiar with the plans. The trip would mark the first visit by a sitting American president to China since Trump's own 2017 state visit during his first term.[1][2]

The visit comes as the world's two largest economies seek to stabilize relations following months of trade tensions, including an $11 billion U.S. arms deal with Taiwan and Chinese military exercises surrounding the island. Trump has described the upcoming trip as a "business trip" aimed at securing further trade wins.[3][2]

items.title: Eight Muslim nations condemn Israel's West Bank annexation moves

featured_image.name: Israel approves biggest expansion of West Bank settlements ...

items.description:
Eight predominantly Muslim countries issued a joint statement on Monday condemning Israel's newly approved measures in the occupied West Bank, calling them illegal annexation attempts that violate international law and threaten regional stability.

The foreign ministers of Turkey, Egypt, Jordan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates denounced Israel's Sunday decision as an effort to impose "unlawful Israeli sovereignty, entrenching settlement activity, and enforcing a new legal and administrative reality in the occupied West Bank, thereby accelerating attempts at its illegal annexation and the displacement of the Palestinian people."[1][2]

The joint statement, posted on the Turkish Foreign Ministry's website, emphasized that "Israel has no sovereignty over the occupied Palestinian territory" and warned that such actions "fuel violence and conflict in the region."[1]

items.title: Ukraine exposes 21 Russian drone makers, says most unsanctioned

featured_image.name: Ukrainian intelligence agency exposes 21 Russian companies ...

items.description:
Ukraine's Main Intelligence Directorate (HUR) has published new data identifying 21 Russian companies involved in developing and producing drones for Russia's war against Ukraine, with officials highlighting that more than half of the listed firms remain free from international sanctions.

The data, released on the HUR's War & Sanctions portal, names manufacturers responsible for producing a range of unmanned aerial vehicles currently deployed against Ukrainian forces and civilians, including cargo drones, first-person-view (FPV) attack drones, and AI-enabled kamikaze systems.[1]
